claim: Moodboards function as decision and communication tools, not decorative inspiration collages.
Internal boards may hold categorized research across imagery, graphics, materials, and effects.
Client-facing boards should be distilled so a small number of references communicate a coherent direction.
References should be interrogated for the specific transferable element rather than copied as whole surfaces.
Reference capture compounds when it is organized into reusable libraries and relationships.
Confirms internal exploration uses category clusters rather than one undifferentiated collage.
Shows one board region answering a specific photography and imagery question.
Shows typography and graphics treated as a separate decision lane.
Shows tactile material cues separated from imagery and type.
Shows effects as a distinct execution variable rather than a vague mood adjective.
Confirms the presentation board is materially sparser than the internal research board.
Shows ongoing reference capture is organized by future decision use, not one giant inspiration feed.
Shows broad collection precedes later project-specific filtering.
Shows relationships between references can be made explicit before execution.
